interface.name: zwlr_layer_shell_v1

description.summary: create surfaces that are layers of the desktop

interface.description: Clients can use this interface to assign the surface_layer role to wl_surfaces. Such surfaces are assigned to a "layer" of the desktop and rendered with a defined z-depth respective to each other. They may also be anchored to the edges and corners of a screen and specify input handling semantics. This interface should be suitable for the implementation of bar UIs, popups, and overlay notifications.

request.name: get_layer_surface

description.summary: create a layer_surface from a surface

request.description:
Create a layer surface from an existing surface. This assigns the surface a role of "layer_surface". A wl_surface can only be assigned a single role. The layer_surface does not take ownership of wl_surface. After destroying a layer_surface on a wl_surface, the wl_surface can still be used to create a new layer_surface.
If the layer_surface is destroyed before the wl_surface object, the wl_surface becomes unbound.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request indicates that the client will not use the layer_shell object any more. Objects that have been created through this instance are not affected.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: wl_surface has a buffer attached or committed

enum.name: layer
enum.description: These values indicate which layers a surface can be rendered in. They are ordered by bottom to top within a single compositor.

interface.name: zwlr_layer_surface_v1
interface.description:
An interface that may be implemented by a wl_surface, for implementations that provide a desktop-style user interface consisting of a background or background-like surfaces.
Each layer surface has a layer it is rendered in and an anchor and margin.
It is the responsibility of the client to set both the size and the anchor. The size is represented by width and height. The anchor is represented by an enum. The margins are represented by a quartet of integers, one for each side.

request.name: set_size

description.summary: sets the size of the surface

request.description:
Sets the size of the surface in surface-local coordinates. The compositor will display the surface centered with respect to its anchors.
If you pass 0 for either value, the compositor will assign it and inform you of the assignment in the configure event.

request.name: set_anchor

description.summary: anchors the surface to the edges of the output

request.description: Requests an edge or point on the surface to be anchored to the corresponding edge of the output. The anchor is a bitmask of top/bottom/right/left. Requests greater than one edge will anchor the surface to multiple edges.

request.name: set_exclusive_zone
request.description: Requests that the compositor avoids occluding an area with other surfaces. The exclusive zone is specified in surface-local coordinates.

request.name: set_margin

description.summary: sets a margin from the anchor point

request.description: Requests that the surface be placed some distance away from the anchor point on the output, in surface-local coordinates.

request.name: set_keyboard_interactivity
request.description: Set to 1 to request that the seat send keyboard events to this surface. For surfaces that are not visible the seat may still send keyboard events.

request.name: get_popup
request.description: Assign this surface_popup a surface. The surface will be entered as a popup for this layer_surface. This case is meant for popups that can be positioned relative to the layer surface.

request.name: ack_configure
request.description:
When a configure event is received, if a client commits the surface in response to the configure event, then the client must make an ack_configure request before the commit request, passing along the serial of the configure event.
If the width or height of the surface changes, it is the client's responsibility to set a new size.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request destroys the layer surface.

event.name: configure
event.description:
The configure event asks the client to resize its surface. If the client does not want to resize, it may ignore the configure event.
The client cannot make a wl_surface.commit. Instead, it must ack_configure and then commit.

event.name: closed
event.description: The closed event is sent by the compositor when the surface will no longer be shown. The client should destroy the layer surface.
